subproblems.title: Translation identity for set integrals of C¹_c functions (FTC + Fubini)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, F ⊆ ℝⁿ a Borel set, ζ : ℝⁿ → ℝ a C¹ function with compact support, w ∈ ℝⁿ and t ∈ ℝ. Then ∫_F ζ(z − t w) dLⁿ(z) = ∫_F ζ(z) dLⁿ(z) − ∫_0^t ( ∫_F Dζ(z − s w)(w) dLⁿ(z) ) ds, where ∫_0^t is the oriented interval integral (∫_0^t = −∫_t^0 when t < 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (ζ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (t : ℝ), MeasurableSet F → ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → ∫ z in F, ζ (z - t • w) = (∫ z in F, ζ z) - ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..t, ∫ z in F, fderiv ℝ ζ (z - s • w) w
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is step 1 (translation identity) of the parent-supplied proof of `codim1_rdo_dg_halfspace_rigidity`, which makes rigorous Simon Ch. 3, 4.3 (8)–(9) (chapter-03.txt lines 664–690; the printed text there only says “it follows that”, so the argument is the parent's step 1 with the details filled in). Here the identity is stated for arbitrary n, a Borel set F, a vector w and t ∈ ℝ.

Notation.
- E := ℝⁿ, L := Lⁿ (Lebesgue measure on E).
- K := tsupport ζ, compact by hypothesis.
- I := [min(0,t), max(0,t)] (Mathlib `Set.uIcc 0 t`) and J := (min(0,t), max(0,t)] (Mathlib `Set.uIoc 0 t`); J ⊆ I.
- G(s, z) := Dζ(z − s w)(w) for (s, z) ∈ ℝ × E.
- Interval integrals are oriented: ∫_0^t h = −∫_t^0 h when t < 0.

1. Dζ is continuous, bounded, and vanishes off K.
   - ζ is C¹, so z ↦ Dζ(z) is continuous (Mathlib `ContDiff.continuous_fderiv`, using 1 ≠ 0).
   - If z ∉ K, then ζ vanishes on the open neighbourhood E ∖ K of z, so Dζ(z) = 0 (Mathlib `support_fderiv_subset`: support Dζ ⊆ tsupport ζ = K).
   - A continuous function vanishing off a compact set is bounded; let M := sup_{y∈E} ‖Dζ(y)‖ < ∞.
   - Consequently G is continuous on ℝ × E (composition of (s, z) ↦ z − s w, of Dζ, and of evaluation at w), |G(s, z)| ≤ M‖w‖ for all (s, z), and G(s, z) = 0 whenever z − s w ∉ K.

2. A compact set carrying all supports.
   - Let K' := {y + s w : y ∈ K, s ∈ I}. It is the image of the compact set K × I under the continuous map (y, s) ↦ y + s w, so K' is compact and L(K') < ∞.
   - If s ∈ I and z ∉ K', then z − s w ∉ K (otherwise z = (z − s w) + s w ∈ K'), so G(s, z) = 0 and ζ(z − s w) = 0.

3. Fundamental theorem of calculus at a fixed point.
   - Fix z ∈ E and set φ(s) := ζ(z − s w) for s ∈ ℝ.
   - The map s ↦ z − s w has derivative −w at every s. By the chain rule (Mathlib `HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt`), φ has derivative Dζ(z − s w)(−w) = −G(s, z) at every s.
   - s ↦ −G(s, z) is continuous by step 1, hence interval integrable on every interval (Mathlib `Continuous.intervalIntegrable`).
   - By the fundamental theorem of calculus for interval integrals (Mathlib `intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt`, valid for both orientations):
     ζ(z − t w) − ζ(z) = φ(t) − φ(0) = ∫_0^t (−G(s, z)) ds = −∫_0^t G(s, z) ds.

4. Joint integrability.
   - Let ν := (Lebesgue measure on ℝ restricted to J) ⊗ (L restricted to F). Both factors are s-finite.
   - G is continuous, hence strongly measurable on ℝ × E.
   - For ν-almost every (s, z) we have s ∈ J ⊆ I, hence |G(s, z)| ≤ M‖w‖·1_{K'}(z) by steps 1–2.
   - The bound (s, z) ↦ M‖w‖·1_{K'}(z) is ν-integrable: it is a constant times the product of the constant 1 in s (integrable for the finite measure on J, of total mass |t|) and 1_{K'}(z) (integrable for L restricted to F, since L(F ∩ K') ≤ L(K') < ∞) (Mathlib `Integrable.mul_prod`); its integral is M‖w‖·|t|·L(F ∩ K') < ∞.
   - By domination (Mathlib `Integrable.mono'`), G is ν-integrable.

5. Splitting the left-hand side. The functions z ↦ ζ(z − t w) and z ↦ ζ(z) are continuous with compact supports (contained in K + t w and K), hence integrable on F (Mathlib `Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport`). Therefore
   ∫_F (ζ(z − t w) − ζ(z)) dz = ∫_F ζ(z − t w) dz − ∫_F ζ(z) dz.

6. Integration over F and Fubini.
   - Integrate the identity of step 3 over z ∈ F and use step 5 (the integral of −h is −∫h):
     ∫_F ζ(z − t w) dz − ∫_F ζ(z) dz = −∫_F ( ∫_0^t G(s, z) ds ) dz.
   - By Fubini's theorem for an interval integral against a measure (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.intervalIntegral_integral_swap`, applied with μ := L restricted to F; its hypothesis is exactly the ν-integrability of step 4):
     ∫_0^t ( ∫_F G(s, z) dz ) ds = ∫_F ( ∫_0^t G(s, z) ds ) dz.
   - Hence ∫_F ζ(z − t w) dz − ∫_F ζ(z) dz = −∫_0^t ( ∫_F Dζ(z − s w)(w) dz ) ds.

7. Conclusion. Adding ∫_F ζ(z) dz to both sides of the last display gives
   ∫_F ζ(z − t w) dz = ∫_F ζ(z) dz − ∫_0^t ( ∫_F Dζ(z − s w)(w) dz ) ds. ∎
proof_key_steps: Dζ is continuous and vanishes off the compact K = tsupport ζ, so G(s,z) := Dζ(z − s w)(w) is continuous, bounded by M‖w‖, and for s ∈ I = [min(0,t), max(0,t)] vanishes off the compact K' = K + I·w.
Pointwise FTC along s ↦ ζ(z − s w) (chain rule, derivative −G(s,z)): ζ(z − t w) − ζ(z) = −∫_0^t G(s,z) ds.
G is integrable for (Lebesgue|uIoc 0 t) ⊗ (L|F), dominated by M‖w‖·1_{K'}(z); ζ(· − t w) and ζ are integrable on F.
Integrate over F, swap the order with intervalIntegral_integral_swap, and rearrange.

subproblems.title: Sign version of the fundamental lemma: nonnegative pairing with all nonnegative C¹_c tests forces f ≥ 0 a.e.
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and f : ℝⁿ → ℝ be locally Lebesgue integrable. Suppose ∫ g(x) f(x) dLⁿ(x) ≥ 0 for every C¹ function g : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support and g ≥ 0 everywhere. Then f(x) ≥ 0 for Lⁿ-almost every x ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ), LocallyIntegrable f volume → (∀ g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ x, 0 ≤ g x) → 0 ≤ ∫ x, g x * f x) → ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, 0 ≤ f x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is the analytic core of step 3 of the parent-supplied proof of `codim1_rdo_dg_halfspace_rigidity` (“This forces f := u(· + tv) − u ≥ 0 a.e.”), stated for an arbitrary locally integrable f. The parent approximates 1_S, S = {f < 0} ∩ B_R(0), by mollified indicators η_{1/j} * 1_S. This proof makes the same three moves:
- approximate an indicator by admissible nonnegative test functions bounded by 1 with uniformly compact supports;
- pass to the limit by dominated convergence;
- conclude from the sign of f on S.
The approximants are smooth Urysohn functions of compact sets K ⊆ S, followed by inner regularity. This is only a change of execution detail: the mollifier API (`ContDiffBump.normed`, `ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable`) is not in the import closure of `GMT.Ch07.Submission` (both are unknown constants there), whereas the smooth Urysohn lemma and inner regularity are. The scheme mirrors Mathlib's own proof of `ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contMDiff_smul_eq_zero` (Mathlib/Analysis/Distribution/AEEqOfIntegralContDiff.lean).

Notation.
- E := ℝⁿ, L := Lⁿ.
- B_R := the open ball of radius R about 0.
- For K ⊆ E and r > 0: K_r := {x : dist(x, K) < r} (open thickening, Mathlib `thickening r K`) and K^r := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ r} (closed thickening, `cthickening r K`).

1. Integrals over compact sets are nonnegative: ∫_K f ≥ 0 for every compact K ⊆ E.
   - Let K be compact. The closed thickening K^1 is closed and bounded, hence compact (Mathlib `IsCompact.cthickening`).
   - Put u_j := 1/(j + 2) ∈ (0, 1) for j ∈ ℕ, so u_j → 0.
   - For each j, K is closed, K_{u_j} is open (`isOpen_thickening`) and K ⊆ K_{u_j} (`self_subset_thickening`).
   - By the smooth Urysohn lemma (Mathlib `exists_contMDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff` for the model 𝓘(ℝ, E), converted with `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`), there is a C^∞ function g_j : E → ℝ with values in [0, 1], support g_j = K_{u_j}, and g_j = 1 on K.
   - Then g_j is C¹ and g_j ≥ 0. Also tsupport g_j = closure(K_{u_j}) ⊆ K^{u_j} ⊆ K^1 (`closure_thickening_subset_cthickening`, monotonicity in the radius), so g_j has compact support.
   - By hypothesis, ∫ g_j f ≥ 0 for every j.

2. Pointwise convergence. Fix x.
   - If x ∈ K, then g_j(x) = 1 = 1_K(x) for all j.
   - If x ∉ K: since K is closed, K = closure K = ⋂_{ε>0} K_ε (Mathlib `closure_eq_iInter_thickening`), so there is ε > 0 with x ∉ K_ε (this also covers K = ∅, where every K_ε is empty). For every j with u_j < ε (all large j, as u_j → 0) we have K_{u_j} ⊆ K_ε, so x ∉ K_{u_j} = support g_j and g_j(x) = 0 = 1_K(x).
   - Hence g_j(x) f(x) → 1_K(x) f(x) for every x.

3. Dominated convergence.
   - For all j and x, |g_j(x) f(x)| ≤ 1_{K^1}(x)·|f(x)|, since 0 ≤ g_j ≤ 1 and g_j = 0 off K^1.
   - The bound is integrable because f is locally integrable and K^1 is compact (Mathlib `LocallyIntegrable.integrableOn_isCompact`).
   - Each g_j f is a.e. strongly measurable (a continuous function times an a.e. strongly measurable one).
   - By dominated convergence (Mathlib `tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence`), ∫ g_j f → ∫ 1_K f = ∫_K f (Mathlib `integral_indicator`; K is closed, hence measurable).
   - Every ∫ g_j f ≥ 0, so ∫_K f ≥ 0.

4. A Borel representative.
   - f is locally integrable, hence a.e. strongly measurable. Let f̃ := `AEStronglyMeasurable.mk f`, a measurable function with f̃ = f L-a.e.
   - f̃ is locally integrable (`LocallyIntegrable.congr`), and set integrals are unchanged: ∫_K f̃ = ∫_K f ≥ 0 for every compact K, by step 1.
   - It suffices to prove f̃ ≥ 0 L-a.e.

5. The negative set is null in each ball.
   - Fix R ∈ ℕ and let S := {x : f̃(x) < 0} ∩ B_R. S is measurable and L(S) ≤ L(B_R) < ∞.
   - Suppose L(S) > 0. Lebesgue measure is inner regular on sets of finite measure (Mathlib `MeasurableSet.exists_lt_isCompact_of_ne_top`, applied with r := 0 < L(S)), so there is a compact K ⊆ S with L(K) > 0.
   - Let h := 1_K·(−f̃). Then h is integrable (f̃ is integrable on the compact K) and h ≥ 0 everywhere, since f̃ < 0 on K.
   - The support of h is exactly K (−f̃ > 0 on K), which has positive measure. By Mathlib `integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg`, ∫ h > 0, i.e. ∫_K f̃ < 0.
   - This contradicts step 4. Hence L(S) = 0.

6. Conclusion. {f̃ < 0} = ⋃_{R∈ℕ} ({f̃ < 0} ∩ B_R) is a countable union of L-null sets, hence L-null (`measure_iUnion_null`). So f̃ ≥ 0 L-a.e., and since f = f̃ L-a.e., f ≥ 0 L-a.e. ∎
proof_key_steps: For compact K, smooth Urysohn functions g_j (0 ≤ g_j ≤ 1, g_j = 1 on K, support g_j = the u_j-thickening of K, u_j ↓ 0) are admissible nonnegative C¹_c tests, so ∫ g_j f ≥ 0.
g_j → 1_K pointwise and |g_j f| ≤ |f|·1_{K^1}; dominated convergence gives ∫_K f ≥ 0 for every compact K.
Pass to a measurable representative f̃. If S = {f̃ < 0} ∩ B_R had positive measure, inner regularity would give a compact K ⊆ S with L(K) > 0 and ∫_K f̃ < 0, a contradiction.
The countable union over R ∈ ℕ gives f̃ ≥ 0 a.e., hence f ≥ 0 a.e.

subproblems.title: Vanishing distributional derivative in direction w gives a.e. invariance under translation by w
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, F ⊆ ℝⁿ a Borel set and w ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose ∫_F Dζ(z)(w) dLⁿ(z) = 0 for every C¹ function ζ : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support. Then for Lⁿ-almost every z ∈ ℝⁿ: z + w ∈ F if and only if z ∈ F.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), MeasurableSet F → (∀ ζ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → ∫ z in F, fderiv ℝ ζ z w = 0) → ∀ᵐ z ∂volume, (z + w ∈ F ↔ z ∈ F)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is step 2 (tangential invariance) of the parent-supplied proof of `codim1_rdo_dg_halfspace_rigidity`, for a single vector w and t = 1; the parent applies this child to each w with ⟨w, v⟩ = 0. It makes rigorous Simon's “it follows that F = ℝⁿ × H” in Ch. 3, 4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 664–690).

Notation. E := ℝⁿ, L := Lⁿ, u := 1_F (the indicator of F), u_w := u(· + w), i.e. the indicator of the Borel set {y : y + w ∈ F}.

1. Translated test functions are admissible. Let ζ be C¹ with compact support, let s ∈ ℝ, and set ζ_s(y) := ζ(y − s w).
   - ζ_s is C¹, being ζ composed with a translation.
   - ζ_s has compact support, being ζ composed with the homeomorphism y ↦ y − s w (Mathlib `HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph`).
   - By the chain rule, Dζ_s(z) = Dζ(z − s w) for every z (Mathlib `fderiv_comp_sub`).

2. The inner integrals vanish. Apply the hypothesis to ζ_s and use step 1: for every s ∈ ℝ,
   ∫_F Dζ(z − s w)(w) dz = ∫_F Dζ_s(z)(w) dz = 0.

3. Translation identity. Apply the sibling lemma `translation_identity` (Lean: `Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_hr_translate_integral_eq`) with this F, ζ, w and t = 1 (note 1·w = w), and use step 2:
   ∫_F ζ(z − w) dz = ∫_F ζ(z) dz − ∫_0^1 ( ∫_F Dζ(z − s w)(w) dz ) ds = ∫_F ζ(z) dz − ∫_0^1 0 ds = ∫_F ζ(z) dz.

4. Change of variables.
   - ∫_F ζ(z − w) dz = ∫ u(z) ζ(z − w) dz (Mathlib `integral_indicator`; F is Borel).
   - Lebesgue measure is invariant under the translation y ↦ y + w (Mathlib `integral_add_right_eq_self`). Substituting z = y + w gives ∫ u(z) ζ(z − w) dz = ∫ u(y + w) ζ((y + w) − w) dy = ∫ u_w(y) ζ(y) dy.
   - Likewise ∫_F ζ = ∫ u ζ.
   - Combined with step 3: for every C¹ compactly supported ζ,
     ∫ ζ(y) u_w(y) dy = ∫ ζ(y) u(y) dy.

5. Fundamental lemma.
   - Every C^∞ function is C¹ (Mathlib `ContDiff.of_le`), so step 4 holds for every C^∞ compactly supported ζ; for real-valued functions ζ(y)·u(y) = ζ(y) • u(y).
   - u = 1_F and u_w are indicators of Borel sets (F, and the preimage of F under the continuous map y ↦ y + w), bounded by 1, hence locally integrable.
   - By the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations (Mathlib `ae_eq_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq`), u_w = u L-a.e.

6. Conclusion. At every z where u_w(z) = u(z), i.e. 1_F(z + w) = 1_F(z), we have z + w ∈ F ⟺ z ∈ F, because an indicator equals 1 exactly on its set and 0 off it, and 0 ≠ 1. Hence z + w ∈ F ⟺ z ∈ F for L-a.e. z. ∎
proof_key_steps: ζ(· − s w) is C¹ with compact support and derivative Dζ(· − s w), so ∫_F Dζ(z − s w)(w) dz = 0 for every s.
The translation identity with t = 1 gives ∫_F ζ(z − w) dz = ∫_F ζ(z) dz.
Substituting z = y + w gives ∫ ζ·1_F(· + w) = ∫ ζ·1_F for all C¹_c ζ, in particular all C_c^∞ ζ.
The fundamental lemma (ae_eq_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq) gives 1_F(· + w) = 1_F a.e., i.e. z + w ∈ F ⟺ z ∈ F a.e.

subproblems.title: Nonpositive distributional derivative in direction v gives a.e. forward invariance along +v
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, F ⊆ ℝⁿ a Borel set and v ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose ∫_F Dζ(z)(v) dLⁿ(z) ≤ 0 for every C¹ function ζ : ℝⁿ → ℝ with compact support and ζ ≥ 0 everywhere. Then for every t ≥ 0 and for Lⁿ-almost every z ∈ ℝⁿ: if z ∈ F then z + t v ∈ F.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), MeasurableSet F → (∀ ζ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ → HasCompactSupport ζ → (∀ z, 0 ≤ ζ z) → ∫ z in F, fderiv ℝ ζ z v ≤ 0) → ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ᵐ z ∂volume, z ∈ F → z + t • v ∈ F
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is step 3 (normal monotonicity) of the parent-supplied proof of `codim1_rdo_dg_halfspace_rigidity`. It makes rigorous Simon's “so that H is non-decreasing on ℝ” in Ch. 3, 4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 664–690), with the parent's sign erratum for the inward normal (the limit set is {⟨z, v⟩ > c}, so mass moves forward along +v).

Notation. E := ℝⁿ, L := Lⁿ, u := 1_F. Fix t ≥ 0 throughout steps 1–5.

1. Admissible translates. Let ζ be C¹ with compact support and ζ ≥ 0. For s ∈ ℝ set ζ_s(y) := ζ(y − s v).
   - ζ_s is C¹, nonnegative, and compactly supported (ζ composed with the homeomorphism y ↦ y − s v; Mathlib `HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph`).
   - Dζ_s(z) = Dζ(z − s v) for every z (chain rule; Mathlib `fderiv_comp_sub`).
   - By the hypothesis applied to ζ_s, for every s ∈ ℝ:
     g(s) := ∫_F Dζ(z − s v)(v) dz = ∫_F Dζ_s(z)(v) dz ≤ 0.

2. The translated integral increases.
   - By the sibling lemma `translation_identity` (Lean: `Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_hr_translate_integral_eq`) with w := v and this t:
     ∫_F ζ(z − t v) dz = ∫_F ζ(z) dz − ∫_0^t g(s) ds.
   - Since 0 ≤ t and −g ≥ 0 everywhere, ∫_0^t (−g(s)) ds ≥ 0 (Mathlib `intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg_of_forall`, which needs no integrability hypothesis), i.e. ∫_0^t g(s) ds ≤ 0 (`intervalIntegral.integral_neg`).
   - Hence ∫_F ζ(z − t v) dz ≥ ∫_F ζ(z) dz.

3. Change of variables.
   - ∫_F ζ(z − t v) dz = ∫ u(z) ζ(z − t v) dz = ∫ u(y + t v) ζ(y) dy, substituting z = y + t v; Lebesgue measure is translation invariant (Mathlib `integral_indicator`, `integral_add_right_eq_self`).
   - Likewise ∫_F ζ = ∫ u ζ.
   - Define f(y) := u(y + t v) − u(y). Then f is Borel and |f| ≤ 1, hence locally integrable; f depends on t but not on ζ.
   - ζ·u(· + t v) and ζ·u are integrable, being bounded, measurable and compactly supported.
   - So step 2 gives
     ∫ ζ(y) f(y) dy = ∫ ζ(y) u(y + t v) dy − ∫ ζ(y) u(y) dy ≥ 0.

4. Nonnegativity of f. Step 3 holds for every C¹ compactly supported ζ ≥ 0. By the sibling lemma `nonneg_fundamental_lemma` (Lean: `Submission.codim1_rdo_dg_hr_ae_nonneg_of_test_nonneg`) applied to f, f ≥ 0 L-a.e.

5. Conclusion. If z ∈ F and z + t v ∉ F, then f(z) = 0 − 1 = −1 < 0. Hence, outside the L-null set {f < 0}, z ∈ F implies z + t v ∈ F. Since t ≥ 0 was arbitrary, the claim holds for every t ≥ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Translates ζ(· − s v) are admissible nonnegative C¹_c tests, so g(s) := ∫_F Dζ(z − s v)(v) dz ≤ 0 for all s.
The translation identity with w = v and t ≥ 0 gives ∫_F ζ(z − t v) ≥ ∫_F ζ.
Substituting z = y + t v gives ∫ ζ·(1_F(· + t v) − 1_F) ≥ 0 for all C¹_c ζ ≥ 0.
The nonnegativity lemma gives 1_F(· + t v) ≥ 1_F a.e., i.e. z ∈ F ⇒ z + t v ∈ F for a.e. z.

subproblems.title: A set a.e. forward-invariant under the half-space of translations {⟨a,v⟩ ≥ 0} is null, co-null, or a half-space
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, F ⊆ ℝⁿ a Borel set and v ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose that for every a ∈ ℝⁿ with ⟨a, v⟩ ≥ 0, for Lⁿ-almost every z ∈ ℝⁿ, z ∈ F implies z + a ∈ F. Then Lⁿ(F) = 0, or Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ F) = 0, or there is c ∈ ℝ with Lⁿ(F Δ {z : ⟨z, v⟩ > c}) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), MeasurableSet F → (∀ a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), 0 ≤ inner ℝ a v → ∀ᵐ z ∂volume, z ∈ F → z + a ∈ F) → volume F = 0 ∨ volume Fᶜ = 0 ∨ ∃ c : ℝ, volume (symmDiff F {z | c < inner ℝ z v}) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. These are steps 5 (density points) and 6 (conclusion) of the parent-supplied proof of `codim1_rdo_dg_halfspace_rigidity`. They make rigorous Simon's “hence (9)” in Ch. 3, 4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 664–690), with the parent's erratum: for the inward normal the limit set is {⟨z, v⟩ > c}, not {⟨z, v⟩ < c}. The hypothesis is exactly what the parent produces in its step 4; no unit-length assumption on v is needed.

Notation.
- E := ℝⁿ, L := Lⁿ; B̄_r(x) is the closed ball.
- θ_r(x) := L(F ∩ B̄_r(x)) / L(B̄_r(x)) ∈ [0, ∞], with division in [0, ∞].
- “r ↓ 0” is the filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ, which is nontrivial.
- A₁ := {x : θ_r(x) → 1 as r ↓ 0} and A₀ := {x : θ_r(x) → 0 as r ↓ 0}.

1. Density points are ordered: if z₁ ∈ A₁ and z₀ ∈ A₀, then ⟨z₀, v⟩ < ⟨z₁, v⟩.
   (a) Suppose instead ⟨z₀, v⟩ ≥ ⟨z₁, v⟩ and put a := z₀ − z₁. Then ⟨a, v⟩ ≥ 0, so by hypothesis N_a := {z : z ∈ F and z + a ∉ F} is L-null.
   (b) For every r ∈ ℝ and z: ‖z − z₁‖ ≤ r ⟺ ‖(z + a) − z₀‖ ≤ r, since (z + a) − z₀ = z − z₁. Hence
       B̄_r(z₁) = (· + a)⁻¹(B̄_r(z₀)) and {z : z + a ∈ F} ∩ B̄_r(z₁) = (· + a)⁻¹(F ∩ B̄_r(z₀)).
       Lebesgue measure is translation invariant for arbitrary sets (Mathlib `measure_preimage_add_right`), so L(B̄_r(z₁)) = L(B̄_r(z₀)) and L({z : z + a ∈ F} ∩ B̄_r(z₁)) = L(F ∩ B̄_r(z₀)).
   (c) F ∩ B̄_r(z₁) ⊆ ({z : z + a ∈ F} ∩ B̄_r(z₁)) ∪ N_a. By monotonicity and subadditivity,
       L(F ∩ B̄_r(z₁)) ≤ L(F ∩ B̄_r(z₀)) + L(N_a) = L(F ∩ B̄_r(z₀)).
   (d) Divide by the common denominator L(B̄_r(z₁)) = L(B̄_r(z₀)). Division in [0, ∞] is monotone in the numerator (Mathlib `ENNReal.div_le_div_right`), so θ_r(z₁) ≤ θ_r(z₀) for every r ∈ ℝ.
   (e) Let r ↓ 0 and use the two limits (Mathlib `le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto'`). This yields 1 ≤ 0 in [0, ∞], a contradiction. So ⟨z₀, v⟩ < ⟨z₁, v⟩.

2. Lebesgue density theorem.
   - F is Borel and L is locally finite on ℝⁿ. By Mathlib `Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet`, θ_r(x) → 1_F(x) as r ↓ 0 for every x outside an L-null set N.
   - If x ∈ F and x ∉ N, the limit is 1, so x ∈ A₁.
   - If x ∉ F and x ∉ N, the limit is 0, so x ∈ A₀.
   - Thus F ∖ A₁ ⊆ N and (ℝⁿ ∖ F) ∖ A₀ ⊆ N.

3. Trivial cases.
   - If A₁ = ∅, then F ⊆ N, so L(F) = 0 (first alternative).
   - If A₀ = ∅, then ℝⁿ ∖ F ⊆ N, so L(ℝⁿ ∖ F) = 0 (second alternative).

4. The threshold c. Assume A₁ ≠ ∅ and A₀ ≠ ∅, and fix z₁* ∈ A₁ and z₀* ∈ A₀.
   - By step 1, ⟨z₀*, v⟩ < ⟨z₁*, v⟩; in particular v ≠ 0 (otherwise both sides are 0).
   - The set S := {⟨z₀, v⟩ : z₀ ∈ A₀} ⊆ ℝ is nonempty and, by step 1, bounded above by ⟨z₁*, v⟩. So c := sup S is a real number.
   - For every z₀ ∈ A₀, ⟨z₀, v⟩ ≤ c (Mathlib `le_csSup`).
   - For every z₁ ∈ A₁, ⟨z₁, v⟩ is an upper bound of S by step 1, hence c ≤ ⟨z₁, v⟩ (Mathlib `csSup_le`).

5. The symmetric difference. Let H := {z : c < ⟨z, v⟩} and P := {z : ⟨z, v⟩ = c}.
   (a) F ∖ H ⊆ N ∪ P. Let z ∈ F with ⟨z, v⟩ ≤ c and z ∉ N. By step 2, z ∈ A₁, so c ≤ ⟨z, v⟩ by step 4. Hence ⟨z, v⟩ = c and z ∈ P.
   (b) H ∖ F ⊆ N. Let z ∉ F with c < ⟨z, v⟩. If z ∉ N, then step 2 gives z ∈ A₀ and step 4 gives ⟨z, v⟩ ≤ c, a contradiction. Hence z ∈ N.
   Therefore F Δ H = (F ∖ H) ∪ (H ∖ F) ⊆ N ∪ P.

6. The hyperplane is null.
   - Since v ≠ 0, P = p + ker⟨·, v⟩ with p := (c/‖v‖²) v (so ⟨p, v⟩ = c) is an affine subspace of ℝⁿ (Mathlib `AffineSubspace.mk' p (ker ⟨·, v⟩)`, membership by `AffineSubspace.mem_mk'`).
   - P ≠ ℝⁿ, because p + v ∉ P: ⟨p + v, v⟩ = c + ‖v‖² ≠ c.
   - A proper affine subspace of ℝⁿ is null for the add-Haar measure L (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.Measure.addHaar_affineSubspace`), so L(P) = 0.

7. Conclusion. L(F Δ H) ≤ L(N) + L(P) = 0, which is the third alternative with this c. Together with step 3, one of the three alternatives always holds. ∎
proof_key_steps: Ordering: if z₁ has F-density 1 and z₀ has F-density 0, then ⟨z₀,v⟩ < ⟨z₁,v⟩; otherwise translating by a = z₀ − z₁ gives θ_r(z₁) ≤ θ_r(z₀) for all r, hence 1 ≤ 0.
Lebesgue density theorem: F ∖ A₁ and Fᶜ ∖ A₀ lie in one null set N.
Otherwise c := sup{⟨z₀,v⟩ : z₀ ∈ A₀} is finite, ⟨z₀,v⟩ ≤ c ≤ ⟨z₁,v⟩ for z₀ ∈ A₀, z₁ ∈ A₁, and v ≠ 0.
F Δ {⟨z,v⟩ > c} ⊆ N ∪ {⟨z,v⟩ = c}, and that proper hyperplane is Lebesgue-null.
